title: post-interview-async-flagging-criteria
content:
Quick personal scratchpad after loop with candidate (Sophie Kim) for Runtime Engineer (mid-senior). This is messy — notes to self for async debrief and recommendation flags.

Context:
- Interview loop: system design (30m) + coding (45m) + culture/pm fit (20m).
- Timeboxed, remote whiteboard + pair-programming on repl.it.
- Candidate has ~5 yrs infra + 2 yrs inference-adjacent (worked on cache layers and batching at prior company).

Raw impressions (brain dump):
- Energy: high, clear communicator, good at surfacing trade-offs.
- Strengths: solid understanding of caching semantics (stale vs strong), good throughput-cost trade-off framing, pragmatic ops focus.
- Weaknesses: limited low-level kernel/quantization experience; code felt a bit hurried — small bugs but fixable.

System design notes (30m):
- Prompt: design a prefix-caching layer for a multi-tenant LLM service that supports partial cache invalidation and tenant isolation.
- Candidate proposed a two-tier cache: per-tenant prefix cache (fast LRU in-memory) + global compressed cache on SSD. Good call on separation.
- Missed: race conditions on cache fill under thundering herd — had to be prompted to consider request coalescing and admission control.
- Security: suggested token-scrubbing at ingress; thought about multi-tenancy via namespace keys. Good.
- Thoughts to capture: strong ops sensibility, could pair well with SRE/design team.

Coding exercise (45m):
- Task: implement simple consistent hashing + eviction hook to push evicted keys to fallback store.
- Candidate implemented hashing cleanly, explained complexity, but forgot to handle concurrent evict/lookup leading to potential double-writes. When prompted, suggested locks but didn't propose lock-free/sharding approach until hint.
- Performance: code was O(1) on average, good docstrings. Minor edge-case bugs that would be caught in PR review.

Culture & collaboration (20m):
- Clear about past on-call responsibilities, structured postmortem example (owned a pager rotation and reduced incidents by 30%).
- Emphasized mentorship, wrote about 1:1 cadence and giving direct feedback.

Score (my internal):
- Technical depth (systems/runtime): 6.5/10 — good design instincts for infra, but less depth on model-specific optimizations (kv cache lifecycles, kernel-level perf).
- Coding: 6/10 — correct, readable; needs polish on concurrency primitives for production paths.
- Communication: 8/10 — concise, trade-off oriented, good at surfacing assumptions.
- Culture fit: 8/10 — aligns with SRE-minded product thinking.
- Overall: 6.75/10 (rounded).

Decision fork I’m leaning toward: recommend a second loop focused on "Inference runtime deep dive" with one senior runtime eng + one infra SRE. Purpose: validate kernel/quantization awareness, heavy KV/cold-start handling, and production concurrency safety. If not available, consider a short take-home on cache-coherence under concurrent loads.

Specific follow-ups/questions for second loop / take-home: (to paste into ask before scheduling)
- Give an example of a kernel-level perf regression you tracked down — what tools and signals did you use?
- How would they reason about quantization/FP16-induced perf/accuracy trade-offs for a model with variable sequence lengths?
- Propose a design to avoid double-fill under high QPS without global locks (expect sharding/admission-coalescing).

Red flags to call out (async):
- Little hands-on with model-serving internals — may require ramping with senior pair.
- Not immediately offering lock-free concurrency patterns (fixable, but think about operational burden).

Suggested async note to hiring panel (copy/paste draft):
"Sophie demonstrated strong ops-first instincts and clear communication. She would likely excel in improving our caching and admission controls and could be a solid mid-senior hire after validating deeper model-serving and kernel-level experience. Recommend a focused follow-up loop (runtime deep-dive) or a short take-home assignment on concurrent cache fill/coalescing. If panel prefers immediate hire, consider pairing hire with senior runtime mentor for first 3 months."

Action items (my TODO):
- [ ] Add short take-home prompt to GH issue and assign to candidate if panel agrees.
- [ ] Ping Marcus for calendar availability for focused deep-dive next week.
- [ ] Upload this note to candidate folder and mark PR-flag in hiring tracker.
- [ ] Add 'kernel/quant' flag to scorecard for this role for future loops.

Other refs/links:
- Confluence draft: hiring/rubric/runtime-lead (compare our kernel/quant expectations)
- Slack thread: #hiring-runtime — share raw takeaways and ask for volunteers.

Notes to self: keep this informal; panel will want crisp bullet summary. Remove speculative remediation language before sharing publicly.
